root_cause.text: The nilfs2 FITRIM handler in `nilfs_sufile_trim_fs` lacks validation of the user-supplied block range, allowing underflow when end_block falls below the first data block, which causes an integer underflow in `nblocks` (a sector_t) that becomes a huge positive value, triggering an excessively long discard operation that holds a lock and leads to a system hang.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "underflow can occur when calculating nblocks if end_block is too small" and "Since nblocks is of type sector_t, which is u64, a negative nblocks value will become a very large positive integer." The patch adds the check `if (end_block < nilfs->ns_first_data_block) goto out;` to safely ignore such invalid input.
